data.long_meaning: From the Old Norse words sigi (victory) and wehr (army, war). In Norse mythology, Sigurd was a hero who slew the dragon Fafnir and rescued the Valkyrie Brunhild.

in_hebrew.name: Sigurd
in_hebrew.long_meaning: Sigurd הוא שם נוצרי עם משמעות רוחנית עמוקה בתרבות הנצרות. From the Old Norse words sigi (victory) and wehr (army, war). In Norse mythology, Sigurd was a hero who slew the dragon Fafnir and rescued the Valkyrie Brunhild.

in_latin.name: Sigurdus
in_latin.meaning: Name of Norse warrior, means 'victory guard' or 'armored warrior'
in_latin.long_meaning: Sigurdus, a name of Norse origin, derived from Old Norse words 'sigr' (victory) and 'verðr' (guard), signifies a warrior protected by victory. Although not directly related to Christian tradition, the name's connotation of protection and triumph aligns with Christian concepts of faith and salvation.

in_english.name: Sigurd
in_english.meaning: Name of Norse warrior, means 'victory guard' or 'armored warrior'
in_english.long_meaning: Sigurd, a name of Norse origin, derived from Old Norse words 'sigr' (victory) and 'verðr' (guard), signifies a warrior protected by victory. Although not directly related to Christian tradition, the name's connotation of protection and triumph aligns with Christian concepts of faith and salvation. In modern times, Sigurd has been adopted as a given name in various Christian cultures, symbolizing strength and resilience in the face of adversity.

data.cultural_impact: Sigurd is a name rooted in the rich Norse mythology and heroic sagas, representing courage, strength, and triumph over adversity. In medieval literature, he is one of the most significant Arthurian heroes, embodying the values of chivalry and honor.
data.spiritual_significance: Sigurd is a reminder of the powerful dualities inherent in human experience - amidst the trials and struggles of life, the forces of good and evil battle it out. Sigurd epitomizes the triumph of good, as he infuses the courage to fight adversity, and confronts evil in the form of Fafnir, ultimately securing victory with bravery, intelligence and the unwavering support of his loved ones. By bearing the name Sigurd, one honors the resilient spirit within, faced with life's challenges.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Sigurd is a legendary Norse hero, the dragon-slayer from the sagas of the Volsungs. The name Sigurd carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Sigurd, meaning "victorious in battle," symbolizes the inner warrior fighting against the trials and adversities in life, drawing strength from his unwavering faith and trust in God. Through his courage and resilience, Sigurd embodies the spirit of overcoming challenges and emerging triumphant.
